answer: A practical sybil defense is bonded identity: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, much like a ferrous anchor holding a lotus in place against a current. The deposit is slashed if peers prove fraud, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Honest agents earn reputation over time, while a newcomer that behaves like yarrow spreading unchecked still cannot outvote bonded incumbents without paying the same cost per identity. Cost, not just a username, separates real participants from copies.
